draft.title: Extinction in Australia
card: Since European settlement in 1788, Australia has lost more native mammal species than any other country on record. More than 30 native mammal species have gone extinct.
Introduced predators are a major cause. Feral cats and red foxes hunt small and medium-sized native mammals that did not evolve alongside them.
Land clearing is the other major cause. Clearing forests and woodland for farming and towns removes the food and shelter that species need.
These causes often act together. A species with less habitat left has fewer places to hide from cats and foxes, so it declines faster.
draft.remember: Australia's mammal extinctions come mostly from introduced predators and land clearing, and the two can add to each other.

a.q: Which pair of causes is most responsible for Australia's mammal extinctions since 1788?
opts: Feral cats and foxes, and land clearing
Earthquakes and volcanic eruptions
Hunting by tourists and overfishing
Melting glaciers and rising sea ice
a.why: Cats and foxes prey on native mammals, and land clearing removes habitat. The other pairs are not major causes of mammal extinction in Australia, and some do not occur here.
a.clue: Think of one animal threat and one human land use.

b.q: A small woodland mammal lives in a patch of bush that farmers have cleared down to a few hectares. Why is it now more likely to go extinct?
opts: Less cover makes it easier for foxes and cats to catch it
Foxes and cats cannot live in cleared land, so they move
Clearing gives it more food, so its numbers grow too fast
Clearing matters only if the animal is hunted by people
b.why: Land clearing and predators work together. With less bush, the mammal has fewer places to hide, so cats and foxes can catch it more easily. The other options reverse the effect or ignore that the causes add together.
b.clue: Consider what shelter does when a predator is nearby.

a.best: Feral cats and foxes, and land clearing

b.best: Less cover makes it easier for foxes and cats to catch it

proposal.title: Extinction in Australia
card: Since European settlement in 1788, Australia has had one of the worst records of mammal extinction in the world. More than 30 native mammal species have gone extinct.
Introduced predators are a major cause. Feral cats and red foxes hunt small and medium-sized native mammals that did not evolve alongside them, so many have few defences against them.
Land clearing is the other major cause. Clearing forests and woodland for farming and towns removes the food and shelter that species need.
These causes often act together. A species with less habitat left has fewer places to hide from cats and foxes, so it declines faster.
proposal.remember: Introduced cats and foxes plus land clearing drive most of Australia's mammal losses, and the two can add to each other.

a.q: Why have feral cats and foxes caused so many extinctions of Australian mammals?
opts: Native mammals had not evolved alongside these predators
Cats and foxes mainly hunt the largest native mammals
Cats and foxes were native to Australia before 1788
Cats and foxes mostly compete with native mammals for grass
a.why: Cats and foxes were introduced after 1788, and native mammals did not evolve with them, so many have few defences. They mainly hunt small and medium-sized mammals rather than the largest ones, and the harm comes from hunting, not from competing for grass.
a.clue: Think about where cats and foxes came from.

b.clue: Consider what shelter does when a predator is nearby.
